== Verify Permissions on SSH Server Public *.pub Key Files
----
To check the permissions of /etc/ssh/*.pub,
run the command:
$ ls -l /etc/ssh/*.pub
If properly configured, the output should indicate the following permissions:
-rw-r--r--
      Is it the case that /etc/ssh/*.pub does not have unix mode -rw-r--r--?
----

discussion:
## Verify Permissions on SSH Server Public *.pub Key Files

To properly set the permissions of `/etc/ssh/*.pub`, run the command: 
```
$ sudo chmod 0644 /etc/ssh/*.pub
```

**Rationale:**

If a public host key file is modified by an unauthorized user, the SSH service
may be compromised.

steps.name: Verify Permissions on SSH Server Public *.pub Key Files
steps.shell:
# Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms
if dpkg-query --show --showformat='${db:Status-Status}' 'linux-base' 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^installed$'; then

find -P /etc/ssh/ -maxdepth 1 -perm /u+xs,g+xws,o+xwt  -type f -regextype posix-extended -regex '^.*\.pub$' -exec chmod u-xs,g-xws,o-xwt {} \;

else
    >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done'
fi

title: Ensure permissions on SSH public host key files are configured (Automated)
